inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = 9M FY2026 actual (7,012 + 7,910 + 9,115 = 24,037) + Q4 FY2026 guidance midpoint 10,250 (Q3 FY26 earnings, Aug-2026). FY2026 ends 25-Oct-2026, one month after the valuation date, so the first discounted year is FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q3 FY2026 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-07-26), 800m. Held FLAT: SBC plus cash taxes on net-share settlement are fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge. Buybacks (FY25 $4.9B, 9M FY26 $1.18B) are the funding mechanism for the flat count and are value-neutral here.
inputs.cash_note: Cash & equivalents 7,037 + short-term investments 2,196 at 2026-07-26 (Q3 FY26 10-Q, XBRL ShortTermInvestments). Total debt 6,444 = senior notes (5,245 non-current + ~1,199 current portion). Long-term investments (5,268) go in the equity bridge, not net cash.
inputs.last_fcf_note: TTM to Q3 FY2026 (Aug-25..Jul-26): OCF 8,396 (FY25 7,958 - 9M25 5,130 + 9M26 5,568) less capex 2,773 (2,260 - 1,475 + 1,988) = reported FCF 5,623; less SBC 701 and equity-award withholding taxes 475 (sbc_incl_equity_taxes 1,176) and interest income 394 = owner FCF 4,053 (13.1% of TTM revenue 30,837). TTM is depressed by a working-capital build and the EPIC-centre capex step-up; FY2024 owner FCF was 6,133 (22.6%), FY2023 6,663 (25.1%).
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts (10-K FY2025, 10-Q Q3 FY2026): ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back) + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation, summed because AMAT publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line. TTM withholding (475) is inflated by the share-price run; FY24/FY25 combined ran 3.2% of revenue, which anchors the forward path.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY2026 repurchases 1,177 (FY2025 4,895; FY2024 3,823). Actual financing outflows, not the ~$12.8B remaining authorization. AMAT is a repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% USD, one rate for all three scenarios: risk-free 4.2% (10y UST) + beta ~1.3 x 4.5% ERP = ~10.0% cost of equity; debt is small against net cash so WACC ~= CoE. Semicap cyclicality is charged in the FLOWS (every scenario carries an explicit WFE digestion downturn) and in the 25% bear weight, so no additional cyclical premium is stacked on the rate (adaptations 7f: charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities (~0.5B) are excluded from net debt. One treatment, consistent.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). AMAT is a US operating company with no bank/REIT/holdco features; it is cyclical, so the adaptations file applies for (d) excluded income -> matching asset, (f) risk charged once, and the mid-cycle margin anchor. CYCLICAL TREATMENT: FY2026E is an AI/HBM/advanced-packaging upcycle year (Q4 guide +51% YoY, Q3 op margin 33.7%, record). Rather than capitalizing peak FCF, each scenario runs 10 explicit years through a digestion downturn (base FY2029 -12%, bear FY2028 -18%) and terminates on a MID-CYCLE adjusted-EBITDA margin (base 33.5% pre-SBC vs FY21-25 range 33.1-33.5% and FY19 trough 27.2%). EBITDA here is PRE-SBC (GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC), because the engine charges SBC separately. First valuation of AMAT: no prior DCF, no memory entry. Q4 FY26 cash generation is not added to the Jul-26 balance sheet (conservative, ~$2/share).

equity_bridge.item: Long-term investments (strategic equity stakes + LT debt securities) at 85% of book
equity_bridge.note: 5,268 at 2026-07-26 (XBRL LongTermInvestments, Q3 FY26 10-Q) less 15% for illiquidity of non-marketable strategic stakes. Matching-asset rule: their gains/interest (other non-operating income 1,237 in 9M FY26) are excluded from the operating flows, so the asset enters the bridge.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.1% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 10.5%, and the 3yr gap is wider (18.7% vs 3.2%). Book value is not a clean growth proxy here: buybacks of $2-6B/yr shrink equity while retained earnings swell it, and FY23-25 revenue was flat through a WFE plateau. Revenue CAGR selected.
historical_growth.notes: Fiscal years end late October. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding tax - interest income): FY2020 2,903, FY2022 3,933, FY2023 6,663, FY2024 6,133, FY2025 4,376 (FY20/FY22 interest income untagged in XBRL and treated as ~0 at near-zero rates). Owner-FCF CAGRs (3.6% / 8.6%) run below reported-FCF CAGRs (7.3% / 11.0%): SBC + withholding grew from 479 (FY20) to 916 (FY25) and interest income on the cash pile rose from ~0 to 406, so a rising share of reported FCF growth is either paid in stock or is treasury income, not operations. FY2025 FCF also absorbed a capex step-up to 8.0% of revenue (EPIC centre) from a 2.5-4.4% FY19-24 range.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +18% takes revenue to ~40.5B, the annualized Q4 FY26 guide run-rate (10.25B x 4 = 41B); FY28 +8% as the HBM/packaging build extends; FY29 -12% digestion (FY19 -12.5%, FY13 -14%, FY09 -38% precedents); then recovery and fade to 3.5% with 3.0% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin: FY21-25 ran 33.1/33.5/32.7/32.5/33.1%; FY26E ~35.5% (Q3 35.4% GAAP-basis EBITDA + SBC). Peak 36% for two years, 31.5% in the downturn (FY19 trough 27.2% was deeper), mid-cycle 33.5% terminal with services mix a modest tailwind offset by China export-control mix loss.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 8.0% FY25 and 8.3% 9M FY26 (EPIC R&D centre, capacity) vs 2.5-4.4% FY19-24; glides to 4.5% as the build completes. D&A catches up from 1.5-1.7% toward 3.0%.
base.tax_rationale: GAAP ETR ~13% FY26 (FDII/FDDEI); cash taxes FY25 1,504 ~16% of pretax. 15% near-term to 16% with Pillar Two pressure.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables + inventory far exceed payables and deferred revenue, so growth consumes ~15% of incremental revenue and downturns release it.

scenario_narratives.base: The AI build carries one more strong year: leading-edge logic (GAA, backside power), DRAM/HBM and CoWoS-class advanced packaging take FY2027 revenue to the Q4 FY26 run-rate (~$40.5B) and FY2028 a little higher, with margins at a 36% pre-SBC peak. Then the WFE cycle does what it has always done: a FY2029 digestion year (-12%) as hyperscaler capex and memory pricing normalize, margins dip to 31.5%, and the business recovers to mid-single-digit growth on a 33.5% mid-cycle margin, with Applied Global Services' installed-base annuity cushioning the trough. China stays structurally smaller (28% of revenue vs 35%) after the memory and mature-node lockout; share loss to Lam/KLA/ASML in 2025 neither reverses nor worsens.
scenario_narratives.bull: The memory supercycle (DRAM shortage through 2027-28, HBM content per bit rising) and advanced packaging (+70% in FY26) extend the upcycle two more years: FY2027 +28%, FY2028 +15%, and the next downturn is a shallow -5% because AGS (22% of revenue) and packaging diversify the cycle. Breadth across deposition, CMP, implant and packaging lets Applied win at every inflection, margins hold 36% mid-cycle, and growth stays above GDP into the 2030s on rising materials-engineering intensity per wafer.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 was the peak. AI capex digestion arrives in FY2028 (-18%, the FY2012-13 pattern), coinciding with a memory price correction and further export-control tightening that removes more China revenue. The 2025 share losses to Lam, KLA and ASML continue into the GAA/backside-power node, pricing power is limited (no ASML-style monopoly step), and mid-cycle margins settle at 31% with capex still elevated from the EPIC build. Growth recovers only to 3-6%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: valuation date sits near the top of an AI-driven WFE upcycle (Q4 guide +51% YoY) with high customer concentration, a single-theme (AI capex) dependency and an open-ended export-control regulator. Base 50% because every scenario already carries an explicit downturn. Bull cut to 25% because it needs the memory supercycle, packaging and share recovery to all go right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AMAT is valued as a cyclical operating company on strict owner FCF (SBC and equity-award withholding tax expensed, interest income stripped with the cash pile and long-term investments added in the bridge), built from components over a 10-year horizon that deliberately runs THROUGH a wafer-fab-equipment downturn rather than capitalizing the FY2026 AI-upcycle peak. The terminal year sits on a mid-cycle 33.5% pre-SBC EBITDA margin (FY21-25 average ~33%) and is capped at 15x owner FCF, the cyclical cap, with Gordon at 10%/3% (~14.7x) the binding bound in the base. Cyclical risk is charged once, in the flows and in a 25% bear weight, not again through a WACC premium. The gap to the market price is the finding: at the current price the market is capitalizing the upcycle as if it were a new plateau, implying either a far lower discount rate or a decade of AI-driven growth without a digestion year, neither of which WFE history supports.
valuation_philosophy.cyclicality_approach: Mid-cycle margin anchor + explicit downturn year in every scenario + 15x cyclical terminal cap + 25% bear weight. No peak-FCF capitalization, no stacked WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Upside risk: AI/HBM/packaging demand proves structural and the next WFE downturn is shallow or skipped; the bull case is then the floor, not the ceiling
Downside risk: AI capex digestion coinciding with a memory price correction (bear FY2028 -18%)
Further US export-control tightening beyond the ~$600M FY26 China headwind
Continued share loss to Lam/KLA/ASML at the GAA and backside-power inflections
Capex step-up (8% of revenue) failing to normalize, holding owner-FCF conversion down
Long-term investment portfolio (5.3B) valuation and liquidity
